market_holds: Spot $4.695 (sealed 18:08 UTC). The event-implied move is 15.5% (front straddle 18.6%, ATM IV 83%). The last two H2 prints gapped -13.0% (Nov 2025, Q4 guide) and -15.4% (Aug 2026, Q3 guide), and the May 2026 print gapped +10.4% (Yahoo daily bars). The stock is down 17% over 20 sessions and about 60% since the 2026-08-25 close of $11.53, in a slow daily grind with no single event (ex-dividend of $0.46 on Sep 9). Peers fell alongside it over the same period: FINV -43%, LX -60%, YRD -74%, LU -53%. Consensus is about $0.46 non-GAAP EPS, which is management's Q3 guide of RMB400-500m non-GAAP NI (-67% to -73% YoY), described as 'largely adopted management's numbers' (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-16). That consensus is stale against the price. At about 123.6M ADS the market cap is about $577M, against equity of RMB24.75B (P/B about 0.17x), cash plus restricted cash plus short-term investments of about RMB10.4B, and a $690M 0.5% convertible due 2030. Guided Q3 profit annualised is a P/E of about 2-3x. Short interest is small and falling: 1.97M ADS at 10/30, 1.0 days to cover. So the decline is longs leaving, not a crowded short. Put/call OI is 0.06. The buyback has been suspended since late June. Management guided C-M2 up about 25% in August and FPD up about 20%, said normalisation takes '2-3 quarters', and gave no Q4 guide yet.
view: Q3 itself is unlikely to be the line. Management called the guide 'extra cautious', carries 472% provision coverage it can lean on, and consensus equals the guide, so a print at or above RMB400-500m non-GAAP is the base case. The stock will trade on three things. First, the Q4 profit guide: the first under the new CEO Zheng Yan, the former CRO, appointed 2026-09-21. Second, the credit trend after the August FPD spike and the collection crackdown. Third, anything on capital return: about $443M of convertible proceeds is still earmarked for buybacks, against a $577M market cap. Forces for a lower Q4 guide: volume fell further after July (-15% vs Q2) and August, online-marketing rules took effect 2026-09-30, the microlending price path runs to 4x LPR by end-2027, Lexin warned of a possible Q3 loss, and a risk-officer CEO has every reason to kitchen-sink. Against that, the price is far below what any plausible Q4 guide in the RMB200-400m range implies (still a low single-digit P/E). Consumer-loan ABS issuance also recovered in Q3 (+20% QoQ in the enterprise ABS market, AAA spreads about 20bp tighter YoY, senior tranches performing; Caixin via cnfin, 2026-11-18), so the funding squeeze management described in August may have eased. Both paths are wide and roughly balanced. A capital-return surprise or a stabilising-credit message on a distressed bellwether could gap it up 10-20%. A Q4 guide near breakeven, or no guide, could take it down another 10-15%. I cannot see which from public data. Qfin reports before FINV, LX and XYF (XYF is due 11-27), so no peer Q3 read-through exists. The one sector Q3 print, Lufax (credit improved but loss quadrupled), saw its stock slide. My view is near a coin flip with a faint negative tilt, from the sector's persistent drift and the new-CEO conservatism.

recommendation.reason: The price (0.17x book, about 2-3x guided earnings, -60% since the Q3 guide) already holds far worse than the stale consensus, so an in-line Q3 is not the line. The Q4 guide and capital return are the line, and I found no dated public evidence of where either lands. Credit and volume evidence after August is negative but already public. Evidence of easing funding is real but indirect and sector-level. Neither side clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 non-GAAP guide at or near the Q3 level, together with a restart of buybacks or convertible repurchases from the remaining about $443M of proceeds, would make the upside case clearly right. A Q4 guide at a loss or withheld, or C-M2 still rising in Oct-Nov, would make the downside right.

self_critique: The case for a confident long is strong and I did not adopt it. The stock trades at 0.17x book and about 3x even a sharply lower Q4 guide. It fell another 12% after the preview with no news. The decline is long capitulation, not shorts. The company has large unused buyback capacity, and a bellwether reporting first can re-rate a capitulated sector on a 'not as bad as feared' call, as May's +25% day showed. Against that, the negative path has also played out twice in a row on H2 guides, with a new risk-officer CEO, and the sector keeps sliding. Without dated evidence on Q4 credit or capital return, I am guessing at a crowd I cannot see.
approach_notes: P4 helped: it showed the consensus is stale against the price, so the headline print is not the line. P3's 'freshest data first' found little Qfin-specific data after August (no monthly disclosures), and sector-level ABS and partner-list data turned out to be weak for a single name's overnight gap.
